## Zoning Evaluation: 3400 N Central Park Ave, Chicago IL
**PIN:** 13-23-316-040-0000 | **Parcel resolution:** authoritative (city address records)

---

### 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **RS-3** (Residential Single-Family, Density 3). Verify at the official Chicago Zoning Map: https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning

---

### 2. Can You Build a Two-Flat Here?

**Possibly, but it depends on lot area.** RS-3 permits two-unit buildings in limited circumstances. Under [1], the minimum lot area per dwelling unit in RS-3 may be reduced to **1,500 sq ft per unit** (allowing a two-flat on a 3,000 sq ft lot) *only if* 60% or more of lots on the same block face are already improved with multi-unit buildings, or the property falls within the "Predominance of the Block" boundary (§17-7-0591). This exemption **only allows a two-unit building** — not larger. The lot is 3,616 sq ft per the assessor, which would satisfy the 1,500 sq ft × 2 = 3,000 sq ft threshold, but the block-face condition must be confirmed in the field.

---

### 3. Key Bulk & Density Standards (RS-3)

The retrieved code text covers density standards [1] and side setbacks for adjacent zoning scenarios [2], but the full RS-3 bulk table (FAR, height limit, front/rear setbacks) was **not included in the retrieved ordinance text** for this query. Here is what *is* confirmed:

- **Minimum lot area per unit:** 2,500 sq ft (standard RS-3); reducible to 1,500 sq ft under the block-face exemption for a two-flat [1]
- **Side setbacks (B/C districts abutting R):** Side setback equals what the residential use would require on the abutting R lot [2] — this applies if any adjacent parcel is commercially zoned
- **Off-street parking location:** Cannot be placed in side setbacks or within 20 ft of the front property line [5]

For the full FAR, maximum height, and front/rear setback table for RS-3, consult **Chicago Zoning Ordinance § 17-2-0300** directly at [Chicago Municipal Code online](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/chicago/latest/chicago_il/0-0-0-2644338) or contact the Department of Planning and Development (DPD) at 312-744-5777.

---

### 4. Overlays & Special Designations

| Designation | Status | Practical Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Planned Development | ❌ No | N/A |
| Landmark / Historic District | ❌ No | N/A |
| National Register | ❌ No | N/A |
| Lakefront Protection | ❌ No | N/A |
| Special Service Area | ❌ No | N/A |
| **Transit-Oriented Development (CTA)** | ✅ Yes | Parking relief available (see §5) |
| **ADU-Eligible Area** | ✅ Yes | Coach house / conversion ADU permitted subject to conditions [2][4] |
| **Affordable Requirements Ordinance Zone** | ✅ Yes | ARO obligations triggered on applicable development |
| **Special District** | ✅ Yes | Consult DPD — specific restrictions depend on the special district's ordinance |

Under the ARO zone, there are 6 affordable housing projects totaling 76 units in the Avondale community area, including Hairpin Lofts (25 units) and Milwaukee Ave. Apts. (32 supportive housing units).

**Brownfield note:** Two nearby EPA-listed brownfield sites (BNSF Little Village Paseo Segments 1 & 2) are recorded in the vicinity. Environmental due diligence is advisable before any ground disturbance.

**Flood zone:** FEMA Zone X — minimal flood hazard; flood insurance is generally not required.

---

### 5. Parking Requirement & Transit Reduction

This parcel is in a **CTA transit-served area** (Blue Line Addison station, ~0.25 mi away). Under §17-10-0102-B, the minimum off-street parking requirement **may be reduced by up to 100%** — meaning parking could potentially be waived entirely for a qualifying residential use. [5] addresses where any retained parking must be located (not in side setbacks, not within 20 ft of the front lot line).

**Important:** This is an RS-3 parcel — there is **no FAR, height, or density bonus** from transit proximity. Those bonuses apply only in dash-3 districts (e.g., B1-3, B2-3, C1-3). The transit benefit here is parking relief only.

---

### 6. Coach House / ADU

**Yes — this parcel is in an ADU-Eligible Area**, which is significant. Under [4] (§17-9-0201-F), a new coach house in an RS district requires compliance with [2] (§17-7-0570). Key conditions:

- **RS districts:** A building permit for a new coach house may only be issued if the parcel complies with the ADU-Allowed RS Area standards [4]
- **Height limit:** Coach house may not exceed **22 ft** (including rooftop features) [4]
- **Side clearance:** At least **3 ft of open, unobstructed space** to at least one side property line for the full building length, unless that line abuts an alley or street [4]
- **Parking:** Accessory parking for the principal building may be reduced/waived via administrative adjustment; the coach house itself requires **no accessory parking** [4]
- **Enforcement:** ADU pre-certification is enforced by the **Department of Housing** [2]

For conversion ADUs (basement/attic units), §17-7-0574 may impose additional area-specific limitations — confirm with the Department of Housing's ADU program.

---

### Confidence & Gaps

- **High confidence:** Zoning classification (RS-3), overlay designations, TOD parking relief, coach house height/setback rules, and ADU eligibility — all from authoritative city GIS and retrieved ordinance text.
- **Cannot determine from retrieved text:** Full FAR, maximum building height, front setback, and rear setback for RS-3 — the complete bulk table was not in the retrieved code chunks. Verify these at §17-2-0302 or with DPD before designing.
- **Cannot determine:** Whether the block-face condition for the two-flat exemption is met — this requires a field survey of the block.
- **Assessment data:** No assessed value was available for this parcel from Cook County (assessment history is empty). Estimated annual property tax for 2024 is **$14,876**, primarily to Chicago Public Schools ($8,131), City of Chicago ($3,616), and Cook County ($874).
